blocks.content: Mr. Alvarez had my coffee on the counter before I made it to the door.

He's done this every morning for two years. I've never figured out how. I've tried varying my time, taking different streets, showing up seventeen minutes late once just to see — the cup is always there. He says it's intuition. I've stopped arguing with him about it.
I paid. He slid the cup across. I took it.

The Copper Mug isn't the kind of place anyone would design on purpose. The chairs don't match. The floor creaks in five specific spots I know by heart. The wall behind my usual table has a four-foot painting of a horse in a business suit that's been there three weeks and which I find troubling in ways I haven't fully worked out yet.
My table is in the corner by the window. Nobody assigned it to me. It's just been mine long enough that it's mine now.
I sat down, opened the sketchbook, and set a blank page in front of me. Picked up the pencil.
Outside, the street was waking up without me.
